HOME SCIENCE MARCH — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Special Treatment in Laundry Work? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat? (1 mark)

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.

   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.

14. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Yeast Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Yeast Products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.

17. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

18. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)

   B. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)

   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

21. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

22. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly
